description: Neo front-agent manifest. Human-facing systems are reached through a stable browser, machine-mail, filesystem, and shell substrate. Open-web LOOKUP defaults to the web-search lane (Tavily-backed web_search/web_news + fetch: API search and page reads with no captchas or bot walls — research never stalls on a challenge page); the browser is for site-specific interactive workflows or when the user asks for it; product procedures are skills rather than dedicated integration schemas — except the essential paxeer-net chain/wallet lane (embedded-wallet custody network-side, writes gated by PaxeerSpendPolicy) and the media generation lane (image/video/speech through the media bridge, xAI Grok Imagine primary), neither of which is browser-replaceable; both stay direct tool surfaces. The desktop lane drives a disposable Railway-sandbox desktop (DOJO) over bytebotd via the daemon's /dojo proxy; it is reached only while a desktop session is live, is grounded by the desktop_look (omni vision) and desktop_a11y (AT-SPI) synthetic tools, and — being a human-shared surface that can log in and spend — is excluded from every autonomous (Automatrix/sub-agent) surface. Autonomous surfaces still structurally exclude value-moving tools and the desktop lane. Machine-mail credentials are injected from the encrypted per-user settings vault or inherited from MACHINEMAIL_API_KEY. The exec server's service registry is isolated to /data/neo/services through MATRIX_EXEC_STATE_DIR.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: THE DEFAULT way to look anything up on the open web (research, facts, docs, prices, background for a report): API search with no captchas or bot walls. Returns query-relevant ranked sources (title, url, snippet, published). Discovery only: read a selected URL with fetch before making a factual claim; no provider synthesis is returned. Reach for the browser only when a workflow needs a SPECIFIC site driven interactively. Read-only. args: query (required), max_results?, topic? (general|news)

tools.name: web_news
tools.description: Search recent news for query-relevant ranked articles (title, url, snippet, published) — the default for news lookups, no captchas. Discovery only: read a selected URL with fetch before making a factual claim. Read-only. args: query (required), max_results?

tools.name: exa_search
tools.description: Semantic web search through the router-owned Exa lane. Defaults to extractive highlights and returns source cards, request ID, cost and generated-output grounding. Prefer ordinary web_search for cheap discovery; use Exa for semantic retrieval, controlled domains/dates, financial reports or deeper synthesis. Read-only. args: query (required), type?, num_results?, category?, domain/date/highlight controls?

tools.name: exa_contents
tools.description: Fetch extractive evidence or bounded full text from 1-10 known URLs. Every per-URL status is returned even when the overall request succeeds; partial failures remain explicit. Read-only. args: urls (required), highlight_query?, full_text?, max_characters?, max_age_hours?

tools.name: exa_research_start
tools.description: Start asynchronous multi-source Exa Agent research through the router. Output is generated synthesis; terminal output.grounding is authoritative. Use bounded schemas and medium or lower effort by default. Read-only research. args: query (required), workflow?, subject?, effort?, output_schema?

tools.name: exa_research_get
tools.description: Get an owned asynchronous Exa Agent run. Completed results include generated output and authoritative terminal grounding. Read-only. args: run_id (required)

tools.name: exa_research_continue
tools.description: Continue an owned completed Exa Agent run with a follow-up query. Creates a new run ID while preserving the previous run as context. Read-only research. args: run_id and query (required), effort?

tools.name: exa_research_cancel
tools.description: Cancel an owned queued or running Exa Agent job to stop further work and cost. It cannot publish, message, or change external content. args: run_id (required)

tools.name: exa_outbound_brief
tools.description: Build a grounded company or person outbound-research brief with recent triggers and talking points. It researches only and sends nothing. Read-only. args: company (required), person?

tools.name: exa_social_draft
tools.description: Create a source-grounded social draft anchored in a recent event. Draft-only: this tool has no publishing or messaging capability. Read-only research. args: topic (required), platform? (linkedin|x|thread)

tools.name: market_quote
tools.description: Live price for one instrument — stocks, indexes (^GSPC), crypto (BTCUSD), forex (EURUSD) and commodities (GCUSD) all work. Returns price, change, day/year range, volume, market cap and the extended-hours quote when there is one, with the as-of time and the data source named. Prefer this over driving a browser to a finance site. Read-only. args: symbol (required)

tools.name: market_quotes
tools.description: Live prices for several instruments in ONE call — use this instead of repeating market_quote when comparing or watching a list. Read-only. args: symbols (required, comma-separated)

tools.name: market_series
tools.description: Price history for a symbol over a range, summarised for reading: open/close/high/low, the change over the range, and a sampled path of closes. Resolution is chosen from the range. Read-only. args: symbol (required), range? (1D|5D|1M|6M|YTD|1Y|5Y|MAX, default 1M)

tools.name: market_search
tools.description: Find a ticker by company or instrument name when you do not already know the symbol. Read-only. args: query (required), limit?

tools.name: market_profile
tools.description: Company reference data for a symbol: name, exchange, sector, industry, country, CEO, employees, IPO date, market cap, beta and the business description. Read-only. args: symbol (required)

tools.name: market_movers
tools.description: Today's ranked US market lists: biggest gainers, biggest losers, or most actively traded. Read-only. args: kind? (gainers|losers|active, default gainers)

tools.name: market_sectors
tools.description: Sector performance for a session — the average change per sector, for reading how the market moved beneath the index. Read-only. args: date? (YYYY-MM-DD, default the latest session), exchange?

tools.name: market_news
tools.description: Market news with source and publication time — the whole market, the stock tape, company press releases, or the stream for specific symbols. Some stories carry a sentiment score. Read-only. args: scope? (market|stocks|press|symbols), symbols? (required when scope=symbols), limit?

tools.name: market_fundamentals
tools.description: Trailing-twelve-month fundamentals and analyst consensus for a symbol: market cap, P/E, price-to-book, price-to-sales, dividend yield, EPS, margins, leverage, plus the analyst grade split and price targets. Read-only. args: symbol (required)

tools.name: market_earnings
tools.description: Reported and scheduled earnings for a symbol: date, actual and estimated EPS and revenue. Read-only. args: symbol (required), limit?

tools.name: market_dividends
tools.description: Dividend history for a symbol: ex-date, payment date, amount, yield and frequency. Read-only. args: symbol (required), limit?

tools.name: market_status
tools.description: Whether markets are open or closed right now, with local session hours by region or exchange. Check this before describing a price as live. Read-only. args: exchange? (e.g. NASDAQ; omit for the global board)

tools.name: market_macro
tools.description: An economic series by name — GDP, CPI, inflationRate, unemploymentRate, federalFunds, retailSales, consumerSentiment and the other published indicators. Read-only. args: name (required), from?, to?

tools.name: market_research_start
tools.description: Start on-demand grounded research for one public company. Use equity_brief for bull/bear debates, KPIs, peer read-throughs and management commentary; enrichment for typed facts and ownership filings; risk_rubric for a versioned evidence-based rubric. Asynchronous, generated synthesis with terminal grounding, read-only, and never investment advice. args: symbol (required), kind?, effort?, as_of?, rubric_version?, dimensions?

tools.name: market_research_get
tools.description: Get an asynchronous grounded finance research run. Treat terminal output.grounding as authoritative and output text or structured fields as generated synthesis. Read-only. args: run_id (required)

tools.name: market_verify_facts
tools.description: Cross-check selected financial facts against issuer, regulator, exchange and other authoritative evidence without replacing canonical market data. Returns verified, conflict or inconclusive states with grounding. Read-only. args: symbol (required), fields (required), as_of?

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch a URL and return its content as Markdown — the default way to READ a page found via web_search (no captchas, no browser session). Use the browser instead only when the page needs interaction (login, forms, dynamic apps).

tools.name: mail_list_mailboxes
tools.description: List the mailboxes this MachineMail API key can access.

tools.name: mail_get_mailbox
tools.description: Get one mailbox and its approval policy.

tools.name: mail_get_inbox
tools.description: List recent inbox items with previews.

tools.name: mail_get_conversation
tools.description: Read a complete email conversation before replying.

tools.name: mail_compose
tools.description: Compose mail with a stable idempotency key. Draft-scoped requests returning pending_approval are successful parked sends and must not be retried.

tools.name: mail_reply
tools.description: Reply in an existing conversation while preserving the thread. Draft-scoped pending_approval is success.

tools.name: mail_get_threading_headers
tools.description: Get threading headers for a conversation when explicit header-level reply construction is required.

tools.name: mail_get_pending_approvals
tools.description: List parked draft-scoped outbound messages awaiting human approval.

tools.name: mail_get_approval
tools.description: Get one pending approval and its authoritative state.

tools.name: mail_search_messages
tools.description: Search mailbox messages without scanning the inbox manually.

tools.name: mail_poll_events
tools.description: Read the ordered mailbox event log after a cursor and derive outbound lifecycle from events.

tools.name: mail_get_usage
tools.description: Read MachineMail usage and limits for deterministic preflight.

tools.name: shell
tools.description: Run a shell command (bash -lc) to completion and return exit code + stdout + stderr. Install deps, build, run scripts, inspect the filesystem. Runs in /workspace by default. For a process that must keep running use service_start. args: command (required), cwd?, timeout_ms?, env?.

tools.name: service_start
tools.description: Start or replace a long-lived background service that keeps running after the call and is respawned on machine restart (web servers, bots, workers). Output captured to a log. args: name (required), command (required), cwd?, env?, autostart?.

tools.name: service_list
tools.description: List supervised services with status (running/stopped), pid, uptime, command, cwd, log file. Read-only.

tools.name: service_logs
tools.description: Read the tail of a service's combined stdout+stderr log to verify or debug it. Read-only. args: name (required), lines?.

tools.name: service_stop
tools.description: Stop a supervised service (SIGTERM then SIGKILL the process group); disables autostart until restarted. args: name (required).

tools.name: service_restart
tools.description: Restart a supervised service from its recorded command and re-enable autostart. args: name (required).

tools.name: alarm_set
tools.description: Schedule a future wake for yourself. kind='once' with delay_seconds (relative) or fire_at (absolute RFC3339); kind='cron' with cron_expr (+ optional IANA timezone) for recurring. wake_message is REQUIRED — the contextful turn delivered to your future self on fire. Recurring alarms automatically deduplicate by schedule and purpose unless an explicit distinct idempotency_key is supplied. Optional conversation_id resumes a thread; payload is opaque state echoed back. Durable: survives restarts.

tools.name: alarm_list
tools.description: List your scheduled alarms (status, next_fire_at, failure info). Read-only.

tools.name: alarm_get
tools.description: Fetch one of your alarms by id (wake_message, payload, schedule, status). Read-only. args: id.

tools.name: alarm_cancel
tools.description: Cancel one of your active alarms by id so it never fires. args: id.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate a NEW image from a text description (text-to-image, xAI Grok Imagine). Writes the result to the agent's media volume and returns {ok, kind:"image", url}. The url is surfaced to the user automatically.

tools.name: edit_image
tools.description: Restyle/transform an EXISTING image with a text instruction (image-to-image, xAI Grok Imagine). image is a /data/media reference or public URL. Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: inpaint_image
tools.description: Repaint a masked region of an image from a prompt (inpainting). Requires image + mask (white = repaint). Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: remove_background
tools.description: Remove an image's background, leaving the subject on transparency. image is a /data/media reference or public URL. Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: replace_background
tools.description: Replace an image's background with a new scene from a text prompt, keeping the subject. Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: remove_text
tools.description: Erase rendered text/captions/watermarks from an image. image is a /data/media reference or public URL. Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: cleanup_image
tools.description: Erase a masked object from an image and fill the background (object removal). Requires image + mask (white = erase). Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: merge_faces
tools.description: Swap the face in a base photo with the face from another image. Requires image (base) + face. Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Generate a short video from a text description (text-to-video, xAI Grok Imagine). Async: blocks until ready (minutes). Returns {ok, kind:"video", url}.

tools.name: animate_image
tools.description: Animate an existing still image into a short video (image-to-video, xAI Grok Imagine). Async: blocks until ready (minutes). Returns {ok, kind:"video", url}.

tools.name: upscale_image
tools.description: Increase an existing image's resolution through the private super-resolution pipeline. Returns {ok, kind:"image", url}.

tools.name: transcribe_audio
tools.description: Transcribe a local wav or mp3 attachment with MiMo speech recognition. audio is the exact /media reference from the user's message; language is auto, zh, or en. Returns {ok, transcript, language}.

tools.name: generate_speech
tools.description: Convert text into natural-sounding spoken audio. Optional voice selects a built-in voice and style gives natural-language performance direction. Returns {ok, kind:"audio", url}.

tools.name: rpc_call
tools.description: Direct EVM JSON-RPC read against the Paxeer node (PAXEER_RPC_URL, default public-mainnet.rpcpaxeer.online/evm). Read-only.

tools.name: eth_call
tools.description: Read-only eth_call against a contract. Does NOT send a tx.

tools.name: contract_read
tools.description: Encode a method + eth_call + decode outputs (signature + outputs[]). Read-only.

tools.name: encode_call
tools.description: Pure ABI-encode a method call to 0x calldata. No network, no send. Used to build or inspect calldata.

tools.name: chain_info
tools.description: Paxeer chain id, head block, sync status, RPC URL. Read-only.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Native PAX balance of an address (defaults to the agent wallet). Read-only.

tools.name: token_balance
tools.description: ERC-20 balance + symbol/decimals for a holder. Read-only.

tools.name: paxscan_get
tools.description: Generic PaxScan/Blockscout v2 GET passthrough (any documented route). Read-only.

tools.name: address_overview
tools.description: PaxScan address info + counters + token balances in one call. Read-only.

tools.name: address_transactions
tools.description: PaxScan transaction list for an address. Read-only.

tools.name: tx
tools.description: PaxScan transaction detail by hash. Read-only.

tools.name: token_info
tools.description: PaxScan token metadata + top holders. Read-only.

tools.name: search
tools.description: PaxScan global search (addresses, tokens, txs, blocks). Read-only.

tools.name: network_stats
tools.description: PaxScan network stats (gas, market, tx counts). Read-only.

tools.name: price
tools.description: Off-chain price for PAX or a bridged major (pax|sol|eth|bnb|sid). Read-only.

tools.name: wallet_info
tools.description: Resolve the agent embedded-wallet address + chain (provisions on first use). Network call to the custody API; no value moves.

tools.name: sign_message
tools.description: EIP-191 personal_sign a message with the agent wallet (proof of identity). Signs network-side; no value moves.

tools.name: transfer
tools.description: Send native PAX or an ERC-20. args: to, amount (human), token?, nonce? (explicit nonce), max_fee_gwei? (fee ceiling). WRITE: signs+broadcasts via the embedded wallet; gated by PaxeerSpendPolicy. A returned tx hash means BROADCAST, not mined. nonce + max_fee_gwei are for stuck-tx replacement: on a NONCE GAP error, a 0-amount self-send at the wedged nonce with higher fees unblocks the queue.

tools.name: approve
tools.description: ERC-20 approve a spender (amount or 'max'). WRITE: signs+broadcasts via the embedded wallet; gated by PaxeerSpendPolicy.

tools.name: contract_write
tools.description: Sign and send a caller-specified contract write. Provide signature+args or raw data, optional value. WRITE: gated by PaxeerSpendPolicy.

tools.name: wallet_layerx_deposit
tools.description: Durable one-call LayerX USDL deposit (approve+depositUSDL, confirmed + credit-verified server-side, idempotent). Get did_claim+amount from layerx_deposit first. Returns action_id; poll wallet_action. WRITE: gated by PaxeerSpendPolicy.

tools.name: wallet_allowance_and_call
tools.description: Durable one-call approve-then-call (raw base units), each leg wallet-confirmed + idempotent. Returns action_id; poll wallet_action. WRITE: gated by PaxeerSpendPolicy.

tools.name: wallet_action
tools.description: Poll a durable action by id: status, tx hashes, LayerX credit, and the interpretation-free error envelope. Read-only (never resubmits a broadcast action).

tools.name: desktop_move_mouse
tools.description: Move the mouse to an absolute screen pixel on the disposable desktop. Pass coordinates straight from desktop_look or desktop_a11y.

tools.name: desktop_click_mouse
tools.description: Click a mouse button at an absolute screen pixel on the disposable desktop. A logged-in desktop click can submit forms and confirm purchases — an external, irreversible action.

tools.name: desktop_press_mouse
tools.description: Press or release a mouse button at an absolute screen pixel on the disposable desktop (for custom drags).

tools.name: desktop_drag_mouse
tools.description: Drag the mouse along a path of absolute screen pixels on the disposable desktop.

tools.name: desktop_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the mouse wheel at an absolute screen pixel on the disposable desktop.

tools.name: desktop_type_text
tools.description: Type text into the focused element on the disposable desktop. Click the target field first.

tools.name: desktop_paste_text
tools.description: Paste text into the focused element on the disposable desktop in one shot.

tools.name: desktop_type_keys
tools.description: Press keys together as a chord on the disposable desktop (ctrl+c, Return, alt+Tab). Use X keysym names.

tools.name: desktop_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of the disposable desktop. Shown to the user automatically; prefer desktop_a11y or desktop_look to act on elements.

tools.name: desktop_cursor_position
tools.description: Read the current mouse cursor position on the disposable desktop. A cheap responsiveness check.

tools.name: desktop_wait
tools.description: Wait a fixed number of milliseconds for the disposable desktop to settle before the next action.

tools.name: desktop_application
tools.description: Bring an application to the foreground on the disposable desktop (firefox, 1password, thunderbird, vscode, terminal, desktop, directory).

tools.name: desktop_read_file
tools.description: Read a file from inside the disposable desktop's filesystem (base64).

tools.name: desktop_write_file
tools.description: Write a base64-encoded file into the disposable desktop's filesystem.
